title: Episodic Memory for Persistent Language Agents
text: Long-running language agents lose task context as interactions accumulate. Episodic retrieval stores compact interaction traces and recalls them by semantic similarity. On multi-session tasks, retrieval improved goal completion but occasionally surfaced stale observations.
evidence: Episodic retrieval stores compact interaction traces and recalls them by semantic similarity.
claim: Episodic retrieval establishes a semantic-recall baseline for persistent agents, but the trace store can surface stale observations.

title: Reflective Memory Consolidation in Autonomous Agents
text: Unfiltered episodic stores accumulate redundant traces and retrieval interference. Reflective consolidation clusters related experiences into durable summaries before later retrieval. Consolidation reduced interference on long-horizon planning, although summarization removed some task-specific detail.
evidence: Reflective consolidation clusters related experiences into durable summaries before later retrieval.
claim: To reduce interference in unfiltered episodic stores, reflective consolidation compresses related experiences into durable summaries, trading task detail for cleaner recall.

title: Graph-Structured Memory for Tool-Using Agents
text: Flat similarity retrieval often misses dependencies among tools, observations, and goals. Graph memory represents these dependencies as typed edges and traverses them during recall. The graph improved multi-step tool use but introduced maintenance overhead as memories changed.
evidence: Graph memory represents these dependencies as typed edges and traverses them during recall.
claim: Where flat similarity retrieval misses dependencies, graph memory uses typed-edge traversal to improve multi-step tool use, at the cost of maintenance overhead.

title: Conflict-Aware Retrieval for Agent Memory
text: Recency and similarity alone can retrieve mutually inconsistent memories. Conflict-aware retrieval attaches temporal validity and contradiction links to stored claims. It reduced contradictory answers in changing environments while increasing retrieval latency.
evidence: Conflict-aware retrieval attaches temporal validity and contradiction links to stored claims.
claim: Where recency and similarity retrieve inconsistent memories, conflict-aware retrieval adds temporal validity and contradiction links, reducing inconsistent answers while increasing latency.
